Thanks Marissa — read through their mark. High-level legal framing: Acme's requests currently broaden the definition of consequential/indirect damages and carve out a list that would swallow our cap if accepted as written. We should avoid unlimited exposure (especially for data incidents). Two drafting options below you can present.

Option A — Legal-preserving (preferred):
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, neither party shall be liable to the other for any consequential, incidental, punitive, exemplary, or special damages, including lost profits, loss of data, loss of goodwill, or similar economic losses. The aggregate liability of each party arising out of or related to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (i) $1,000,000 or (ii) the fees paid to Supplier under the applicable Order Form in the 12 months preceding the claim."

Option B — Commercial compromise (strategic customer):
"Except for liability arising from (i) gross negligence or willful misconduct, or (ii) a certified data security incident that results in unauthorized access to or destruction of customer data, neither party shall be liable for consequential or indirect damages (including lost profits, loss of data, loss of goodwill). For certified data security incidents, Supplier's aggregate liability shall be capped at the lesser of (x) $5,000,000 or (y) twice the fees paid under the applicable Order Form in the prior 12 months; for all other claims, the general cap applies (greater of $1,000,000 or 12-month fees)."

Negotiation notes:
- For (ii) above we should require objective criteria: written incident report within 30 days, root-cause analysis, and (where applicable) third-party forensics.
- Avoid open-ended "loss of data" without tying it to a breach attributable to us.
- Consider a de-escalation path: if Acme insists on unlimited, escalate to Laura/SE and offer a short-term SLA credit instead of broad financial exposure.

I'll drop tracked changes into the redline doc and a plain-text snippet you can share.

—Aditya
